original_post_text:
𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐥𝐢𝐤𝐞 𝐃𝐨𝐮𝐠 𝐏𝐨𝐥𝐤 𝐨𝐫 𝐧𝐨𝐭, 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐢𝐬 𝐚 𝐰𝐢𝐧 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐓𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐬 𝐏𝐨𝐤𝐞𝐫.

The community knows the truth: when a room gets raided, it’s usually a death sentence. We’ve watched it happen. Copa Club. Watauga. Social Lounge. Wild Cards. Poker House Dallas (now operating as PH Social under new ownership). All of these rooms gone. ￼

Comebacks are rare and what the Lodge just did is historic. They are potentially coming back in three months after being shut down. 𝐓𝐡𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐦𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐡𝐬. That is monumental, and something absolutely nobody thought was possible.

On Monday night I heard through a source the Lodge would reopen June 1st. I said to myself, that’s fake news. No way. Well… here we are.

But beyond the legal win, let’s talk about what nobody else is saying: the employees get to come back to work. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐝𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐫𝐬. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐟𝐟. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐬 who didn’t have to pack up and move to Vegas just to keep food on the table. That’s the real story.

The community showed up with fury, passion, rage, love, and yeah, some hate too. But that’s what families do. Collectively, we gave the Lodge our voice. Let’s keep that same energy every time any room gets shut down anywhere in Texas.

DFW. Austin. Houston. San Antonio. We are one family. What happens to one of us happens to all of us.

The charges were bull. The fight isn’t over. And The Sham Report will be here raising hell every step of the way.

Congratulations to the Lodge. Welcome back. 
— Shomari Williams | The Sham Report

expanded_title: Whether You Like Doug Polk or Not, The Lodge’s Comeback Is a Historic Win for Texas Poker
expanded_deck: When a Texas card room gets raided, it is usually a death sentence — which is why the Williamson County grand jury's decision clearing the way for The Lodge to reopen and bring its dealers and staff back to work matters for every room in the state.
expanded_body:
Originally posted April 29, 2026.

Whether you like Doug Polk or not, this is a win for Texas poker.

The community knows the truth: when a room gets raided, it's usually a death sentence. We've watched it happen — Copa Club, Watauga Social Lounge, Wild Cards, and Poker House Dallas (now operating as PH Social under new ownership). All of those rooms were gone.

Comebacks are rare, and what The Lodge just did is historic. Coming back roughly three months after being shut down is monumental, and something almost nobody thought was possible.

On Monday night I heard through a source that The Lodge was targeting a June 1 reopening. At first I said to myself, "That's fake news — no way." Well… here we are.

But beyond the legal win, let's talk about what nobody else is saying: the employees get to come back to work. The dealers. The staff. The families who didn't have to pack up and move to Las Vegas just to keep food on the table. That's the real story.

The community showed up with fury, passion, rage, love, and yeah, some hate too. But that's what families do. Collectively, we gave The Lodge our voice. Let's keep that same energy every time any room gets shut down anywhere in Texas.

DFW. Austin. Houston. San Antonio. We are one family. What happens to one of us happens to all of us.

The charges were bull. The fight isn't over. And The Sham Report will be here raising hell every step of the way.

Congratulations to The Lodge. Welcome back.

— Sham
author: Shomari Williams

fact_verification_flags.claim: On April 28, 2026, a Williamson County grand jury declined to authorize proposed charges (a no-bill), clearing the way for The Lodge Card Club in Round Rock to reopen
fact_verification_flags.note: Verified by April 28–29, 2026 reporting and Shomari Williams's April 29 commentary.

outdated_info_flags.original_statement: On Monday night I heard through a source the Lodge would reopen June 1st.
outdated_info_flags.current_status: Following the April 28 grand jury no-bill and initial June 1 target date, The Lodge officially reopened in May 2026
outdated_info_flags.editorial_note: Describes the initial target reopening window reported on April 29, 2026.
